title: Recurring motifs in my dreamworld - how many of them do you guys share?
content: When I was 7, the I-90 bridge across Lake Washington collapsed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacey_V._Murrow_Memorial_Bridge#1990_disaster I think that idea was the nucleus of my dreamworld. It started out as a dream version of Seattle centered around the fragmented ruins of the bridge. In my dreams the bridge isn't always completely gone, but often is closed to cars, or falling apart, or the tunnel on the Seattle side of the lake is a series of labyrinths filled with construction crews. I have dreams about a farmer's market taking place in the middle of the freeway, having to abandon my car and walk home across Mercer Island, etc. But the dreamworld expanded from there. I have a quite detailed dream version of Seattle and Bellevue (on the east side of the lake) and a more vague version of the surrounding area. It is broadly geographically similar but the particulars are quite different from real life. Different versions of neighborhoods I know, different relationship of one place to another, landmarks that are entirely invented alongside unrecognizable versions of things from real life. Like for many people here, there is a mall. For me it's on a hill above downtown. The mall is contiguous with an airport and a train station, a hospital and a giant parking garage. It's all interconnected in strange ways - for example, there's a three-story Barnes and Noble in the top few floors of the mall that you need to walk through to get to the connector skybridge to the train station. There's a giant dimly lit swimming pool connected to the parking garage, much deeper than any actual swimming pool, inside a strange concrete room that's shaped like a huge cube. But a lot of the adventuring takes place outside. Walking around through different neighborhoods, exploring different downtowns, driving or taking trains from one city to another, taking ferries out to the islands, hiking on trails through the mountains.. the mountains are closer than in real life. I have a lot of travel dreams simply about getting from one place to another, often in the company of a group of people. Sometimes I'm hopping from giant rock to giant rock following the course of a huge river. Sometimes I'm driving and the road becomes too steep or narrow for my car and I need to clamber up a washed out cliff to get where I need to go. Some of my best dreams are just ones where I am walking through an odd and wonderful forest for hours. At the beach, which also is at a consistent location from dream to dream, in this case out at the Pacific coast, there are always tsunamis every few hours. This used to be scary, but now is a fact of life, something that can be planned around. They are always beautiful and powerful and terrible in an awe-inspiring way. I can climb to a high vantage point and watch them wash over the beach and up into the forest. But it all feels like it spreads out from the broken bridge... like that's the nucleus, the mythic artifact, the seed. That's what linked up the settings from my dreams into the patchwork quilt that I visit most nights, even if I am often not aware in a particular dream of where I am. I wouldn't say that these dreams are good dreams, but they're not bad dreams either. The mall dreams, the city exploration dreams, they are all about working through something or seeking something or trying to avoid something. They are process dreams and sometimes they are satisfying, sometimes disappointing. I feel wistful and worked up in a strange way thinking about them - the emotions are strong but they are ones that I would have a hard time describing even if they didn't dissolve leaving me confused when I awaken.
